lede: Stuart ran one of the busiest front offices in the league — 113 adds, 115 winning claims, five trades — and ended with the team most shaped by its draft. 64% of the production came from players drafted in October, and the best of them, Jamal Murray at $28, banked 2,758. A 10–9 record, seventh seed, a 4–5 playoff loss to Fantastic 5, and a win in the fifth-place game.
profile: A guard team, and a pure one. Free-throw percentage won 18 of 21 matchups, first in the league at .835. Assists and steals at 71%, threes at 62%. The cost is two categories conceded almost every week: blocks 3–18 and rebounds 3–17–1. It is the mirror image of Brighton. Giving up two categories before tip-off means needing five of the remaining seven — which is exactly how a team that wins 4.6 a week finishes 10–9.
ledger: 97 of 189 categories, with a bye in week 21. The close weeks show the problem. Nine matchups came down to one category, and Masters went 4–5 in them, including the playoff loss to Fantastic 5. The early season was the high point: 8–1 over Ben's Need Some VC in week 2, and 6–3 or better in weeks 6 to 8.
draft: The top of the draft was the season. Murray ($28) banked 2,758, Donovan Mitchell ($41) 2,595, LaMelo Ball ($20) 2,073 and Austin Reaves ($30) 1,676. Ball and Murray returned over 95 per dollar and stayed all year. Cason Wallace at $1 was the bargain: 726 per dollar, kept to the end. The misses were bigs, which fits the profile. Kristaps Porzingis ($19) started seven games before being traded on day 20, and Deandre Ayton ($12) went on day 93. Khris Middleton ($4) never appeared in a lineup — he was on BC KO by day 4.
production:
Only 36% from outside the draft. The four most productive players were all drafted, and the best acquisitions sit well down the list: Alperen Sengun (851 in 24 games), Payton Pritchard (761) and De'Anthony Melton (646).

For all the claims and trades, the in-season additions were supplements rather than the team.
trades: Five trades, all recovered, net −901 in production. The costliest came first: day 12, Grayson Allen for Trae Young, −898. Young played ten more games for anyone, Allen 45. The best was day 20, Porzingis and Tari Eason for Sengun, +504 — and then Sengun was moved on day 97 for Pritchard and Shaedon Sharpe (−73). Day 121, Coby White and Mark Williams for Dillon Brooks, came out −504, with Brooks playing seven games.
wire: The volume was enormous: 115 winning claims from 488 attempts. The return was mid-table — 0.67 net production a day per swap, 5th of 14, 55% hit rate — on a top bid of just $6. $11 of FAAB was left unspent. The best move was a brave one: day 95, Egor Demin in for Trae Young, +10.1 a day, cutting the name for the production.
bench: Thirty wasted player-days and 742 production on the bench — the most in the league. Week 13 accounts for four of the six biggest: LaMelo Ball 55 and Jimmy Butler 47 on day 87, Sengun 40 and Ayton 40 later that week, in a matchup lost 3–6. Ball appears three times in the top six. Some of that is a crowded roster with more starters than slots. But for a team living on five-of-seven weeks, 742 benched is the most avoidable number on this page.
last: The fifth-place game against The Infirmary, played properly: 50 starting slots set against 38, nine of nine on the last day, and a 6–3 win. Points 810 to 507, assists 190 to 87 — the guard build doing what it was built to do.
closing: The paradox of this season is that a manager this active had a team so decided by its draft. The guards bought in October — Murray, Mitchell, Ball, Reaves — were the season. Everything after added movement more than production: trades net −901, and the wire mid-table despite the volume. Two changes would matter most. Lineup attention first — the league-leading 742 benched is the cheapest improvement available. Then a decision on the bigs: conceding blocks and rebounds every week makes every matchup a five-of-seven, and that is how nine one-category weeks ended 4–5. The guard core is good enough. One real centre held all season would have changed the math.
